title: Building a Complete Kotlin Application
subtopics: Testing, Packaging, and Preparing for Deployment
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of building a complete kotlin application using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates building a complete kotlin application.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Building a Complete Kotlin Application** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Apply building a complete kotlin application by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Organizing Application Layers, Integrating External Services, Testing, Packaging, and Preparing for Deployment—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with organizing application layers. Then compare it with integrating external services. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Organizing Application Layers
items.text: Organizing Application Layers is one part of building a complete kotlin application. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Testing, Packaging, and Preparing for Deployment
items.text: Testing, Packaging, and Preparing for Deployment helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in the project that declares the necessary JVM, coroutine, networking, database, or serialization dependencies. Never commit real secrets.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Building a Complete Kotlin Application removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of building a complete kotlin application in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates building a complete kotlin application. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving organizing application layers.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain building a complete kotlin application without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Organizing Application Layers. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
